1571	
1572	Every command prints what it produced first, then a one-line outcome (✓ or
1573	✗), and its problems last: diagnostics, errors and warnings with their help
1574	and notes, then the error and warning count. On a terminal the output is
1575	coloured and paths are marked `+`/`-`; piped or with `NO_COLOR`, it is plain

1578	| Command | Behaviour |
1579	| --- | --- |
1580	| `piton check [paths...]` | Validates syntax, imports, references, types, inheritance, composition, exports and circular dependencies, reporting errors and warnings. Writes nothing. Exits 0 when there are no errors and 1 otherwise. Paths are optional files, directories or globs; the default is the project (or every `.pi` file under the working directory when there's no `piton.config.pi`). |
1581	| `piton build [config] [--dry-run]` | Builds the project configured by `piton.config.pi` (or the given config). Writes renderer output to `<output>/<path under root>.<ext>` (defaults: `./dist`, JSON), so `spec/components/Button.pi` becomes `dist/components/Button.json`: the entry file plus every file holding something the entry's exports reference. A registered framework's output replaces it unless the config sets `output` or `renderer`, which asks for both. Records every file in `.piton/manifest.json`. The whole plan is validated before anything is written. `--dry-run` reports without writing. |
1582	| `piton compile <path> [--renderer json\|yaml\|markdown] [--write] [--dependencies]` | Compiles one file to stdout (JSON by default): one key per export. `--write` writes `<file>.<ext>` next to each input and is required for globs. `--dependencies` wraps the result as `{"value": "<compiled output as a string>", "dependencies": [absolute source paths]}` so build tools know what to watch; bundled package files are left out. |

1677	   - one exported anchor per file, named after the file;

1683	   - prose in string blocks, and structure in keys and lists;

1708	
1709	Checked with `piton compile` and `piton build`:
1710	
1711	- The CLI has a few things the spec doesn't name: `build --dry-run`,
1712	  `tether --as`, agent argument passthrough, the `reach` flags, and

**/home/hyphyphyph/piton/repl/src/prompt_mode.rs**
- **Selection state (`HistoryList`, ~505–625):** three new fields: `selectable`, `selected: BTreeSet<usize>` (indices into `tasks`) and `last_selected` (where a shift-click range starts). Only `HistoryList::tasks()` turns `selectable` on; previous answers pass `false`.

  - `clear_selection()` (620).
  - Because `task_history` is already swapped by `swap_session`, each project keeps its own selection with no extra code.
- **Row actions:** `render_row` and `render_row_as` take a new `actions: Vec<AnyElement>`, shown at the row's right (`ml_auto`) as siblings of the toggle, so clicking them never opens or closes the list. The two ask-list rows pass `Vec::new()`; the tasks row passes `self.render_selection_actions(cx)` (5164).
- **Checkbox:** in `render_list` (~876 and `.children(checkbox)`), each heading gets a checkbox before `task_summary`. The new helper `history_checkbox` (5493) wraps a gpui-kit `Checkbox` and calls `cx.stop_propagation()`, so clicking it doesn't open the item. Shift is read from `window.modifiers().shift`. The element id for tests is `("history-select", ix)`.
- **Batch send (2501–2600):**
  - `selected_for(to)` lists the selected tasks whose `other_mode` is `to`, oldest first. Chain and unknown-mode tasks never qualify.
  - `send_selected_to(to)` shows one "No project open" notification if there's no project. Otherwise it calls the existing `send_to_other_mode` for each task in order, then deselects only the tasks it sent.
  - `render_selection_actions` builds the row's "N selected" label, the "Send N to Spec" and "Send N to Code" buttons (label and icon tinted with `mode_color`, each shown only when it has something to send) and "Clear".
- **Queue ordering:** several sends in a row queue correctly without new code. `start` sets `working = true` synchronously, so the first send starts and the rest go through `enqueue` in order. `send_next` only sends the first queue item once it has been saved.
- **History reload (2769):** after the history reloads, selected indices past the end of the task list are dropped.

**/home/hyphyphyph/piton/repl/src/prompt_queue.rs**
- New `stamp()` (32) always returns a later value than the previous call, and new `add_at(queued_at, …)` (50) saves at that stamp. `add` is now `#[cfg(test)]` and delegates to `add_at`.
- **Why:** queue files were named with the time taken after the compile finished, so prompts queued back to back (as a batch does) could reload in the wrong order after a restart.

- **`previous_tasks_can_be_selected_and_sent_to_the_other_mode` (9419):** a real UI test. It covers:

  - Clear;

- **Formatting:** I applied rustfmt only to my own code. `prompt_mode.rs` still has one unformatted spot (the `closing.question` block, ~4510), which was already unformatted before my change.

Every task in the previous tasks list now has a checkbox, and you can send the selected tasks to the other mode in one go. The new tests pass when I run them, and nothing is committed.

**How it works** (spec added under `previousTasks` in `spec/scope/prompt-mode/index.pi`; check, format check and build all pass):
- **Selecting:** each task's heading has a checkbox before its status. Clicking it doesn't open or close the task, and shift-click selects a range. The selection stays when you close and reopen the list, until you send or clear it.
- **Actions on the "Back to the latest task" row:** while anything is selected, the right end of the row shows:
  - "N selected";
  - "Send N to Spec", which sends the selected Code tasks;
  - "Send N to Code", which sends the selected Spec tasks;
  - "Clear".

  Each Send button is tinted the colour of the mode it sends to and shows only when the selection has tasks it would send. Chain tasks and tasks with no recorded mode can be selected but aren't sent.
- **Sending:** each task goes through the same path as the single Send to Spec/Code button, oldest first, so they wait in the queue in their original order. Tasks that were sent are then deselected, and the list stays as it was.

**Code:** almost all of it is in `src/prompt_mode.rs`. The selection belongs to previous tasks only, so the previous answers list has no checkboxes. Each open project keeps its own selection.

**Queue fix in `src/prompt_queue.rs`:** queued prompts were stamped with the time they finished compiling, not when they were queued. Prompts queued back to back, as a batch does, could come back in the wrong order after a restart. They're now stamped when queued.

**Choices you might want to change:**
- Shift-click only adds to the selection; it never deselects.
- "N selected" counts every selected task, including Chain tasks; the Send buttons count only what they would send.

**Worth knowing:**
- **History order:** saved history files are named down to the second only, so tasks saved within the same second can reload in random order. In practice runs take longer than that. I didn't change the file format.
- **Tests:** three new tests pass: a UI test for selecting and sending, an end-to-end test that runs a batch in order, and a queue-order test. The full suite fails only on `defaults_are_this_repositorys_templates`, which was already failing, and `selected_answer_text_can_be_copied_or_attached`, which fails only some of the time.
- **Uncommitted usage fixes:** the usage-popover fixes from last time (`src/chat_input.rs`, `src/harness.rs`, `src/usage.rs`, including the fix for Codex double-counting) are still uncommitted, alongside this change.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors still need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings, and the `backlog` MCP server still can't connect because its executable isn't on your PATH.
